item.title: Coastal Flooding Causes Driveway Collapse at Nicolas Cage’s SoCal Mansion
item.description: The driveway of a coastal mansion in Malibu owned by actor Nicolas Cage collapsed Tuesday morning, opening up a giant hole in front of the house. The mansion was damaged during a Los Angeles-area coastal flooding advisory over lingering effects of Marie, which had been a hurricane before turning back into a tropical storm. The collapse caused a gas leak just before 6 a.m., prompting authorities and a utility to respond.

item.title: Anthropic Researchers’ Dire Safety Warnings Prompt Call for New AI Rules
item.description: lawmakers this week called for new rules to govern AI, after an Anthropic researcher went public with his concerns about the technology escaping human control. The reaction was broader than after previous statements from OpenAI and Anthropic staffers about safety concerns, drawing input from lawmakers who do not often forcefully engage in debates over how to govern AI. Commerce Department, the agency with in-house AI safety researchers.

item.title: Nearly 100% Chance of a Mediterranean Tsunami Within Next 30 Years
item.description: On June 22, 2022, the organization stated that “the probability of a tsunami wave exceeding 1 meter in the Mediterranean in the next 30 years is close to 100%.” That estimate concerned an event somewhere in the Mediterranean basin over the following three decades, roughly through 2052. What UNESCO’s Mediterranean Tsunami Warning Means The Mediterranean is often treated as an unlikely setting for a tsunami. A tsunami could hit the French Riviera before a warning reaches people on the beach, according to a UNESCO alert.

item.title: Man pleads guilty to fraud and forgery offences relating to fake takeover approach
item.description: Christopher Woolcott has pleaded guilty to 4 counts of fraud and forgery after creating a fake takeover bid for Touchstone Exploration Inc. Mr Woolcott held shares in Touchstone Exploration Inc and stood to benefit financially from any upward movement in the share price had the fake takeover bid been announced to the market. Mr Woolcott admitted creating a fictitious takeover approach for Touchstone Exploration Inc using multiple false identities and forged documents, in an attempt to lend credibility to the approach.

item.title: 29 Companies Joined The Unicorn Board In August, Led By AI Software And Semiconductors
item.description: A total of 29 companies joined The Crunchbase Unicorn Board in August, adding around $63 billion in value to the board. Nine companies exited the Unicorn Board in August, per Crunchbase data: Three that went public — the most notable being Unitree Robotics — and six via acquisition, including Hugging Face , OpenRouter and Airtable . The Crunchbase Unicorn Board is a curated list that includes private unicorn companies with post-money valuations of $1 billion or more and is based on Crunchbase data.

item.title: How To Measure An Innovation Economy: South Korea
item.description: This week in Seoul, we presented the latest application of that work: The Innovation Economy of South Korea. Ignore them and you miss a large part of the real economy’s innovation capacity, particularly in ecosystems — Korea among them — where corporate-led and government-backed innovation has historically mattered as much as the VC route. At Mind the Bridge , we are regularly asked to put numbers on something that is, by nature, hard to pin down: the health of an innovation ecosystem.

item.title: Risks becoming more global and volatile, value of reinsurance never more evident: Munich Re
item.description: Munich Re, one of the world’s largest reinsurance companies, has underscored that the value of reinsurance has never been more evident than it is today, as risks continue to become more global and volatile. Thomas Blunck, Member of the Board of Management, Munich Re, commented: “The value of reinsurance has never been more evident than it is today. At the 2026 Monte Carlo at the Rendez-vous event, Munich Re described reinsurance as society’s immune system, but cautioned that the industry is facing an abundance of uncertainties from the changing climate, geopolitical tensions, and rapid technological development.

item.title: Catastrophe bond market shifts further towards indemnity triggers and per-occurrence coverage
item.description: Over the last year and through the record-levels of issuance in 2026 so far, the catastrophe bond market’s outstanding exposure has shifted further towards indemnity triggers and per-occurrence coverage, as preference for these types of deals continues to rise, both on the sponsor and investor side. While catastrophe bond issuance has been increasing rapidly in recent years, the triggers used for cat bonds have moved towards a clear preference for indemnity protection. Which leads nicely onto a discussion of the growing preference for exposure to per-occurrence covers in the catastrophe bond market, as naturally a growing sponsor base of primary insurers prefer to utilise cat bond coverage in that form so that plays into this market dynamic as well.

item.title: Marsh launches new European D&O insurance facility
item.description: Global professional services firm Marsh has launched Unity D&O, a new European directors and officers (D&O) insurance facility for private and public organisations with revenues up to €1 billion. To streamline placement for organisations, the solution features a harmonised pan-European policy wording with local underwriting and claims support, underpinned by Marsh’s proprietary D&O. Unity D&O has been developed with these priorities in mind.” Unity D&O complements Marsh’s wider suite of financial and professional lines capabilities, including the Marsh Alpha, Cyber Unity, D&O Echo, and Cyber Echo facilities, and forms part of Marsh’s continued development of pan-European solutions across multiple lines of business.

item.title: MNK Group acquires Danish non-life insurer ETU Forsikring
item.description: MNK Group, the independent international insurance group, has completed the acquisition of 100% of Danish insurer ETU Forsikring A/S, following approval from the Danish Financial Supervisory Authority (Finanstilsynet). According to the announcement, MNK Group’s main focus is to strengthen ETU as a Danish insurer. Established in 2006, ETU is a Danish non-life insurer and is headquartered in Rødekro, Southern Jutland.

item.title: Carbon adds Phil Wooldridge as Head of US Casualty and Deputy Active Underwriter
item.description: Carbon Underwriting Limited, a delegated authority underwriting specialist with its own Lloyd’s syndicate, has appointed Phil Wooldridge as its new Head of US Casualty and Deputy Active Underwriter, effective 28 September 2026. In his new role, Wooldridge will grow Carbon’s book of business for US policies covering long-tail casualty risks. In the past, Wooldridge was the Head of London US Casualty at SiriusPoint Ltd.

item.title: Amazon Seen as Shielded from Liability for Miami Cargo Plane Crash
item.description: When the cargo plane came to rest 1,300 feet past the end of the runway at Miami International Airport, its nose sat flush with the ground, the tail — and the billboard-sized Amazon.com Inc. Like the logos emblazoned on thousands of blue Amazon delivery vans ferrying packages around the US, the plane smile was something of a contrivance — a branding opportunity. The jet was operated by 21 Air, a North Carolina-based cargo carrier that flies eight aircraft for Amazon.

item.title: Oregon Proposes 2.1% Increase in Pure Premium Workers’ Comp Rates for 2027
item.description: The increase to the average pure premium rate would contribute to an increase in the average cost of workers’ comp coverage, from 89 cents per $100 of payroll in 2026 to 92 cents per $100 of payroll in 2027. Related: Oregon Disabling Workers’ Comp Claims Fell in 2024 The rise in Oregon’s average pure premium rate is due to benefits for workers injured on the job being increased through Senate Bill 1519 2026 passed in 2026, which modified weekly lost-time wage compensation benefits for workers with disabling claims. A proposal from the Oregon Department of Consumer and Business Services calls for the pure premium rate to increase by an average 2.1%.

item.title: New York Proposes Rule to Require Prior Approval of Auto Insurance Rate Hikes
item.description: New York officials are moving to require auto insurers to receive prior approval before implementing any increases in private passenger insurance rates. The new rate regulation will require insurers to seek express prior approval from DFS before implementing any upward rate changes. Currently, under the state’s “flex-rating” system, insurers may implement no more than two overall average private passenger auto rate increases without the department’s prior approval if the cumulative effect of the rate increases are within 5%.

item.title: BPL launches new surety business line
item.description: BPL, an independent credit and political risk insurance broker, has launched BPL Surety, a new business line designed to support corporates and financial institutions seeking solutions for global guarantee requirements. Our track record and experience in surety means this new business line is ideally positioned to add value to clients and the surety market, understanding what underwriters want and how to deliver those solutions to all parties,” said Parrott. The business line will respond to a recent increase in appetite from underwriters for new types of applications, as well as the opportunity to bring these solutions to a wider client base.

item.title: Verisk releases Fraud Discovery platform connecting intelligence, analytics, and investigations
item.description: The post Verisk releases Fraud Discovery platform connecting intelligence, analytics, and investigations appeared first on Insurtech Insights . Verisk has announced Verisk Fraud Discovery, a fraud prevention platform that unifies fraud intelligence, advanced analytics, network analysis, digital media forensics, and case management into a single, scalable solution. Verisk’s approach helps create greater visibility into potential fraud networks and further strengthens our evolving fraud prevention capabilities.” The platform combines fraud intelligence, analytics, network analysis, digital media forensics, and investigation workflows to help organisations uncover hidden relationships across people, organisations, policies, and claims, and detect opportunistic, organised, and coordinated fraud activity.

item.title: insureMO and Gallagher Philippines accelerate digital insurance distribution
item.description: insureMO has announced the successful launch of its API-led insurance distribution platform to support Gallagher’s expanding digital insurance distribution capabilities across various ecosystems in the Philippines. The collaboration with insureMO strengthens Gallagher’s digital distribution capabilities across affinity, banking, embedded insurance, financial services, and other emerging channels. insureMO provides Gallagher with a technology foundation that brings together insurance product configuration, digital customer journeys, APIs, and carrier connectivity.

item.title: HelmGuard raises $7.3 million
item.description: AI-powered security and compliance platform HelmGuard AI has raised $7.3 million in seed funding. HelmGuard uses AI agents to collect and assess risk information from source systems, automate third-party risk reviews and monitor the behavior of other AI agents. HelmGuard has offices in London, New York and San Francisco and was co-founded by former Palantir executive John Daley.

item.title: Agero partners with MOTER
item.description: Agero, through its Urgently acquisition, announced a partnership with insurance software and data company MOTER Technologies. The collaboration pairs Urgently’s digital roadside assistance platform and Agero’s nationwide service network with MOTER’s connected vehicle intelligence, claims visualization, and driver risk technologies. By combining Urgently’s digital roadside assistance platform, Agero’s nationwide network and accident management expertise, and MOTER’s connected vehicle intelligence, we’re helping insurers and automakers accelerate claims response, improve visibility into vehicle incidents, and deliver more proactive support when drivers need it most.” – Harrison Russell, Chief Client Officer, Automotive at Agero.

item.title: Acrisure introduces Auris AI
item.description: Acrisure has introduced Auris AI, an applied AI platform developed using Palantir technology. Auris AI is designed to support AI-assisted workflows that help our teams surface insights, coordinate tasks, and better serve clients.” – Benjamin Funk, Chief Technology Officer and Chief AI Officer at Acrisure. “Auris AI enables Acrisure to bring AI into the core of its operations while maintaining control over the data, workflows and decisions that power its business.

item.title: Pharmacists Mutual Names Shaw Vice President and Head of Claims
item.description: Pharmacists Mutual Insurance Group named Sharon Duez Shaw vice president and head of claims. Shaw joined the Pharmacists Mutual as part of a planned leadership transition from Peter Lambert, senior vice president, who will retire effective March 31, 2027. Shaw has experience building claims organizations, leading enterprise claims strategy, modernizing litigation and trial strategy and partnering across underwriting, actuarial, and finance functions.

item.title: New Corgi, Liberate, VERVE Claims Tech. Do We Need New Acronyms?
item.description: Corgi Insurance recently launched Corgi Claims, what it bills as a full-service third-party administrator that pairs a national network of more than 5,000 licensed adjusters with an AI that scores severity, flags coverage issues and surfaces missing documents. The service, Corgi says, reviews claims the instant they are reported. Corgi Claims handles major lines of business, including commercial liability, property, catastrophe, renters, trucking, workers’ compensation and specialty programs.

item.title: Washington Commanders Player Scores Workers’ Compensation Win
item.description: The Washington Commanders football team has failed to block a workers’ compensation claim in Maryland by a former defensive tackle injured at the team’s training facility in Virginia just three days after he was signed by the team. In 2024, the Maryland Workers’ Compensation Commission (MWCC) denied the claim filed by player Curtis Brooks for his ruptured left Achilles tendon, finding that he was not a covered employee under Maryland law and thus not entitled to workers’ compensation benefits. The Washington Commanders (officially named Pro-Football LLC) is a Maryland limited liability company that plays its home games in a stadium in Landover, Maryland and has a training field in Ashburn, Virginia.

item.title: CatIQ raises Saskatchewan & Manitoba severe storm outbreak loss estimate to C$923m
item.description: CatIQ, Canada’s insured loss and exposure index provider, has raised its insurance industry loss estimate from the severe storm outbreak that affected Saskatchewan and Manitoba in the Canadian Prairies in early June to CAD $923 million, an 8.5% increase from its second loss estimate of CAD $850 million that was issued in July. We covered CatIQ’s first loss estimate from the severe storm outbreak, where losses had reached CAD $728 million. A severe storm outbreak swept across southern Saskatchewan and southern Manitoba on June 9th and 10th, which generated tornadoes, with hail measuring up to 10cm in diameter and record-breaking rainfall.

item.title: Hiscox Capital Partners leverages cedent relationships to navigate record cat bond issuance: Prabis
item.description: As investor and issuer interest in catastrophe bonds remains high following a record-breaking first half of the year for cat bond issuance, Hiscox Capital Partners is leveraging decades of traditional reinsurance relationships to navigate an increasingly crowded ILS market, Vincent Prabis, Managing Principal of Hiscox Capital Partners told Artemis. Speaking with us in an interview at the Monte Carlo Rendez-vous event, Prabis explained that rather than treating catastrophe bonds as standalone financial instruments, Hiscox Capital Partners approaches the market with the same qualitative underwriting framework applied to its traditional balance sheet business. In light of this significant increase, we asked Prabis to explain how Hiscox Capital Partners is maintaining pipeline quality amidst this influx of capital.

item.title: AXA XL names Rana Gillmon as Head of Private Equity Client Relations, Americas
item.description: AXA XL, the property and casualty specialty risk division of AXA, has appointed Rana Gillmon to the newly created role of Head of Private Equity Client Relations, Americas. In her new role, Gillmon will lead AXA XL’s private equity client engagement across the Americas. Matt O’Malley, Chief Client & Distribution Officer, Americas, AXA XL, commented on the promotion, “Rana’s appointment is an important step forward in how we serve the private equity sector across the Americas.

item.title: Fitch expects strong growth in offshore life reinsurance to continue
item.description: Fitch Ratings expects strong growth in offshore life reinsurance to continue, with Bermuda remaining the dominant primary jurisdiction. Fitch expects some moderation in sales growth for the full year 2026 but expects offshore reinsurance volumes to remain elevated, supported by partnerships between insurers and alternative investment managers, sidecars and block reinsurance transactions. Fitch analyses offshore reinsurance on a case-by-case basis, considering jurisdictional strength, capital standards and transaction structure.

item.title: Mosaic launches AI Lab and Forward Deployed Engineer Programme
item.description: Mosaic Insurance, a global specialty insurer, has announced the launch of an AI Lab and Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) Programme, designed to accelerate practical artificial intelligence (AI) adoption across its business functions. Mosaic’s AI Lab is a new unit working across its businesses to develop and deploy in-house AI capabilities that improve day-to-day operations. The lab is focused on rapid delivery and measurable outcomes across functions, including underwriting, finance and global operations, with senior leadership prioritising use cases aligned with Mosaic’s automation strategy.

item.title: Ledger Hires New Security Chief as Crypto Hacks Hit $1.4 Billion
item.description: Ledger SAS, a maker of hardware devices used to store cryptocurrencies, is combining oversight of its internal technology systems and security under a single executive, as a rise in artificial intelligence-fueled crypto attacks pushes companies to rethink their defenses. Paris-based Ledger has hired Oded Blatman as chief information officer and chief security officer, it said in a statement on Wednesday. Prior to joining Ledger, Blatman served as CIO and chief information security officer at Fireblocks for five years and was formerly global CISO of Bank Hapoalim, one of Israel’s largest banks.

item.title: Private Credit Investors Clash Over £36 Billion BHP Dam Collapse Litigation
item.description: Two litigation funders are backing rival law firms in a fight for control of a £36 billion ($48.8 billion) suit over one of Brazil’s worst environmental disasters. Law firm Pogust Goodhead brought the UK case against BHP Group Ltd and Vale SA on behalf of more than 600,000 Brazilians affected by the 2015 Fundão dam collapse. With the miners found liable in November , the case’s two main financial backers are now at odds over how to maximize the payout — and which lawyers should lead the next phase.

item.title: NATO Allies Foil Russian Subsea Cable Sabotage Plot
item.description: Deep in Arctic waters near the remote Svalbard archipelago this spring, NATO allies caught Russian subs training to unleash a secret weapon designed to disable critical undersea cables without leaving any fingerprints. The deep-sea face-off comes at a time when some Western intelligence officials fear the Kremlin is ramping up sabotage operations in Europe and preparing for a conflict with NATO. The Kremlin consistently denies conducting sabotage operations in NATO countries or plotting any confrontation.

item.title: AXA partners with Publicis Sapient to deploy standardised “Global AI Hub” at scale
item.description: The post AXA partners with Publicis Sapient to deploy standardised “Global AI Hub” at scale appeared first on Insurtech Insights . “Publicis Sapient brings together specialist AI expertise, enterprise AI solutions and global experience that will help us accelerate AI adoption consistently across our organisation, while maintaining the governance and flexibility required in a highly regulated business.” David Murphy, head of financial services EMEA and APAC at Publicis Sapient, said enterprise AI delivered the greatest value when paired with strong engineering foundations. AXA has entered a strategic partnership with Publicis Sapient, a technology firm providing enterprise artificial intelligence (AI) platforms and services, to accelerate the next phase of its AI transformation.

item.title: Insurity Announces Ratio Content and Rating Engine
item.description: Insurity, a provider of software and analytics for the property/casualty insurance industry, announced Ratio Content and Rating Engine, an API-first regulatory content and externalized rating engine for admitted commercial property/casualty carriers. Ratio Content and Rating Engine closes that gap, giving carriers the speed and flexibility to rate the commercial business they actually write.” Ratio Content and Rating Engine turns machine readable bureau content into production ready policy logic and provides the rating performance to support commercial policies. Ratio Content and Rating Engine is source-agnostic and designed to support bureau and carrier-specific content, subject to applicable licensing.

item.title: Estrella Insurance expands to Orange County
item.description: Estrella Insurance has opened its first Orange County agency in Santa Ana, California. The office is owned by Matheus Gould-Alexandre, a former insurance sales agent who is fluent in English, Spanish and Portuguese. Tustin Avenue, the agency offers auto, homeowners, renters and Mexico auto insurance.

item.title: AI in Portfolio Management: A Tool, Not a Decision Maker
item.description: By grounding portfolio management in strong data foundations, clear decision ownership and well-defined analytical pillars, insurers can apply AI in a targeted way that reinforces judgment, improves governance and accelerates action rather than replacing it. (Image source: IIR.) Portfolio management is a critical discipline for P&C insurers seeking sustainable profitability in an increasingly complex market. Done well, portfolio management enables data-driven decisions that protect margins and guide growth, even when data is imperfect.

item.title: NYC Officials Feared Liability Over Toxic Air After 9/11 Attacks
item.description: 11, 2001, attacks, including documents showing officials were weighing potential liability from toxic exposure while trying to reassure the public about the safety of Lower Manhattan. One memo prepared in October 2001 for Robert Harding, a deputy mayor under Rudy Guiliani, estimated that the city could face 35,000 potential plaintiffs and contemplated seeking federal protection from “toxic tort cases that might arise in the next few decades.” Another city document from May 2002 said that officials would avoid using the word “risk” in correspondence about a cleanup program because doing so “would defeat the purpose of creating public confidence.” An estimated 400,000 people, including first responders, were exposed to toxic contaminants and other hazards in the days, weeks and months following the attacks, according to the CDC. Fires in the towers’ debris piles burned for months after the attacks, releasing carcinogenic byproducts.

item.title: Retrocession set for comeback as conditions evolve. Collateralized tail protection stable: S&P
item.description: Retrocession is back in fashion as market conditions evolve across reinsurance and rating agency S&P believes retro buying is set for a comeback, as reinsurers recognise favourable pricing and conditions for protection, while looking to manage their catastrophe limits in a softening market. S&P said that “retrocession is set for a comeback as market conditions evolve.” As of January 1st 2026, S&P’s benchmark reinsurance group on average ceded roughly 50% of their exposure to a 1-in-250 year event. “Reinsurers that successfully balance growth ambitions with risk mitigation will be well positioned to protect capital strength and navigate the next phase of the reinsurance cycle.” But, despite this capital strength across the reinsurance sector, S&P also notes that reinsurers recognise the opportunity to benefit from softening market conditions to further build their protection through retrocession purchases.

item.title: Industry loss estimate for Saskatchewan and Manitoba severe weather reaches CAD 923m: CatIQ
item.description: CatIQ, the independent Toronto-based catastrophe insurance data provider and subsidiary of PERILS, has revised its industry loss estimate for the severe storm outbreak in Saskatchewan and Manitoba, Canada, to CAD 923 million. The severe weather event took place between June 9 and 10, impacting the Saskatchewan and Manitoba provinces which experienced heavy storms that brought tornadoes, hail, damaging winds, torrential rain and flash flooding, affecting tens of thousands of residents and businesses. Laura Twidle, President and CEO of CatIQ, commented: “Canada experienced severe weather-related loss events at an above-average pace in the summer of 2026.

item.title: Bamboo Insurance Launches Texas Homeowner Program
item.description: Bamboo Insurance announced the launch of its Texas Essential Homeowner Program, a new admitted, flexible product designed to give Texas homeowners greater flexibility in how they structure their coverage. Bamboo Insurance said the structure keeps coverage transparent while providing greater flexibility to insureds to tailor coverage to their individual needs and budgets. The launch builds on Bamboo Insurance’s continued expansion of its product offerings and capacity.

item.title: Higginbotham Acquires Kansas’ Two West Capital Advisors
item.description: Higginbotham announced it has acquired Kansas City, Kansas-based Two West Capital Advisors. Two West will remain based in Kansas City and continue serving its existing clients, with all current teammates on board — and new ones coming in as the firm actively recruits for expected growth. That team will gain the support of Higginbotham’s broader HR, marketing, legal and compliance infrastructure, while Two West employees also become employee-owners in the larger organization.

item.title: Illinois Sues Repair Company for Deceptive Business Practices
item.description: (ABC) for its deceptive business practices that mislead consumers, most often senior citizens, to sign a contract for home repair work at inflated prices by unlicensed technicians while they also unknowingly waive their statutory rights to cancel the contract. Raoul’s lawsuit claims ABC violates the Illinois Consumer Fraud Act, Deceptive Trade Practices Act and the Illinois Home Repair and Remodeling Act. Illinois Attorney General Kwame Raoul last week filed a lawsuit against ABC Plumbing, Heating, Cooling & Electric, Inc.

item.title: Allstate Trains Adjusters in Damaged Homes
item.description: Source: Allstate.) Allstate (Northbrook, Ill.) has built two full-scale homes inside its Claims University training center to help property claim adjusters learn how residential damage occurs, spreads and is repaired. Allstate says the homes include standard-grade components and higher-end materials to help adjusters prepare for varied property conditions and repair considerations. The homes recreate residential damage scenarios that adjusters may encounter when helping homeowners recover from property damage.

item.title: Singapore’s DBS Faces $1 Billion Lawsuit in Alleged 1MDB-Linked Claim
item.description: DBS Bank is being sued for an estimated S$1.298 billion ($1.03 billion) in damages linked to the multibillion-dollar 1MDB scandal, Southeast Asia’s largest lender DBS Group said on Wednesday. In July last year, liquidators trying to recover money from 1MDB sued Standard Chartered Bank in Singapore, alleging it enabled fraud that led to more than $2.7 billion in financial losses between 2009 and 2013. DBS rejected the claim and said it would fight it vigorously, adding that the company has made no provision for the lawsuit.

item.title: Probe Underway in Deadly Amazon Cargo Jet’s Fiery Runway Crash
item.description: The five people killed when an Amazon cargo jet ran off a runway at Miami International Airport were all inside a van carrying seven people from a cleaning company, and an SUV hit outside of airport property, National Transportation Safety Board Chairwoman Jennifer Homendy said Monday. Homendy called the scene of Sunday’s crash “utter devastation.” She didn’t detail how many people were in the SUV or where the dead were located. Federal investigators examining cause of deadly overrun

item.title: Despite Security Concerns, Meta Launches AI Agent Muse
item.description: Meta rolled out on Tuesday a long-touted AI assistant that can autonomously send emails, sell a car and book travel on a person’s behalf, despite internal concerns that the technology mismanages its access to sensitive personal data. The company’s Muse agent, known internally as Hatch, is the centerpiece of CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s plan to supply “personal superintelligence” to the billions of people who use Meta’s services daily. Modeled on the open-source AI agent OpenClaw, Muse is designed to access a person’s apps across categories like email, calendar, payments, health, shopping and the smart home, Meta said.
